question.text: A coaxial cable consists of an inner wire of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi></math> surrounded by an outer shell of inner and outer radii <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>b</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>c</mi></math> respectively. The inner wire carries an electric current <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>i</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math> which is distributed uniformly across cross-sectional area. The outer shell carries an equal current in opposite direction and distributed uniformly. What will be the ratio of the magnetic field at a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></math> from the axis when <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>i</mi></mfenced></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo><</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>i</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mo><</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo><</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi></math> ?
